:JUDGMENT:
The Petitioners have filed the Petition against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of Ranganathappa S/o. Late.

Doddarangappa in a Road Traffic Accident.
2. The brief averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 13.02.2023 at about 6.15 a.m., the deceased Ranganathappa was proceeding towards Dharmasthala by walk on the extreme left side of the road near Chikkamma Doddamma temple, 100 meter back from KB Halli village, Chikkamagaluru, at that time a tanker lorry bearing No.KA-20- C-6077 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, came from behind and dashed against the Ranganathappa.
Due to the forced impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Prior to the date of accident, the deceased Ranganathappa was hale and healthy and he was an agriculturist and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
3. The Petitioners have further contended that the accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of tanker lorry by its driver.
Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the tanker lorry
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
4. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, they appeared before the court through their respective counsels and filed objections to the main petition.
In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.1, denied the negligent driving by the driver of tanker lorry.
He contended that the driver of the lorry tried to avoid the accident and took the vehicle to the right.
Further he contended that his vehicle was insured with the Respondent No.2.

On these Krishnamma vs Chandrashekar M.S on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179380877/
2 grounds, the Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

sentences.text: In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.2, denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.

Further it contended that owner of the insured lorry has not intimated the alleged accident to this respondent and there is violation of Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it contended that, the driver of the lorry was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
Further it contended that the deceased sustained injuries and died because of the accident caused by some unknown vehicle in a hit and run case.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
5. On the rival pleadings, the following Issues have been framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the Petitioners prove that they are the legal representatives of the deceased?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that Ranganathappa S/o Late Doddarangappa died due to injuries sustained by him in an accident occurred on 13.02.2023 at about 6.15 a.m., near Chikkamma- Doddamma temple, 100 meter back, KB hall village, Chikkamagaluru, arising due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tanker lorry bearing Reg.
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

4. What Order or Award?
6.
In order to prove the case, the Petitioner No.2 got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 15 documents as per Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-15 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 examined a witness as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed its side evidence.
7. Heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioners and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.
I have perused the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record.

8. My answer to the Issues are as under :
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.

 REASONS 9. Issue No.1-

It is the case of the Petitioners that the one Ranganathappa who is the husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioner No.2 and 3 was died in the Road Traffic Accident caused by the driver of the offending tanker lorry bearing No.KA-20-C-6077.
On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry.
10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.2 has been examined as P.W.1 and got marked 15 documents as per Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-15.

Ex.P-1 to Ex.P11 are the true copies of FIR,
Complaint, Intimation, spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, Inquest panchanama, PM report, notice issued under Sec.133 of IMV Act, reply to notice and Charge sheet.

11. Upon going through the said documents, Ex.P.1 and 2 i.e., FIR and Complaint show that the case was registered against the driver of the offending tanker lorry for the offence punishable under Section 279, 304A of IPC r/w Sec. 187 of MV Act.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of intimation.
Ex.P.4 and 5 are the true copy of Spot mahazar and sketch which show that the concerned police prepared sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.

The exact spot of the accident is marked in the sketch, which shows that the accident was taken place at the edge of the road, wherein the deceased was walking by that time the offending tanker lorry came from behind and dashed against the deceased.
This shows the negligence of the driver of the offending tanker lorry.
Ex.P.6 is the IMV report which shows that the cause of accident is not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in the accident.
Ex.P.7 is the Inquest mahazar.
Ex.P.8 is the PM report, which shows that cause of death is due to cranio cerebral damage as a result of injury sustained to head consequent upon blunt heavy force/surface Impact.
All the injuries are ante mortem in nature and fresh at the time of death.
Ex.P.9 is the notice under section 133 of MV Act and Ex.P.10 is the replay to the said notice.
Wherein the owner of the offending lorry i.e., respondent No.1 had admitted that the accused shown in the charge sheet was the driver of the offending lorry at the time of accident.
Wherein he also furnished DL and other documents pertaining to the vehicle.

Ex.P.11 is the true copy of the Charge-sheet, which shows that the I.O has submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of tanker for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 304A of IPC r/w Sec.187 of MV Act.
Ex.P.12 to 15 are the notarized copy of Aadhar card of petitioners and deceased.
12. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.1 has cross examined the P.W.1 in lengthy.
In the cross-examination PW.1, he admitted that he is not the ey witness to the accident.
Hence, his evidence is not deciding factor for negligence aspect is concerned.
13. The respondent No.1 has examined a witness who is the official of the TRO, Shimogga as RW.1 and got marked authorisation letter and copy of DL extract at Ex.R.1 and 2.

In his examination in chief he deposed that the driver of lorry i.e., Sudhir.D was issued a Hazardous goods vehicle license Krishnamma vs Chandrashekar M.S on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179380877/
4 for the first time on 28.02.2020.
There is no information in Ex.R.2 till which year the said license is valid.
However, the Hazardous License issued on 28.02.2020 is valid for a period of 3 years, i.e. till 27.02.2023.
The said license was renewed from 17.02.2023 to 16.02.2024.
Since the license of the said driver's heavy goods vehicle expires in the year 2024, the Hazardous Goods License will also expire in the same year.
The renewal of the Hazardous Goods License will be on the HGV License itself.
Hazardous Goods License is issued for a period of 3 years for petroleum product goods vehicles.
Their office will have a file to show whether the driver had a valid Hazardous Goods License on the date of the accident.

He has admitted that the driver of lorry i.e., Sudhir had a valid license to drive a hazardous goods vehicle on 13.02.2023.
14.
Though the Respondent No.1 denied the negligence driving of his driver he has not chosen to examine his driver to rebut the evidence of the petitioners.
As such he has no evidence to prove his contention.
Moreover, after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending tanker, which is not challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.

Therefore,
having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-20-C-6077 and in the said accident, husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioner No.2 and 3 succumbed to injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the "Affirmative".
15. Issue No.1 and 3:
Both these issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid the repetition of the facts.
16. It is stated in the Petitions that the Petitioner No.1 is wife and petitioner No.2 is son and Petitioner No.3 is daughter of the deceased Ranganathappa.
In order to prove this fact, PW.1 has produced Ex.P12 to 15 Aadhar cards of the petitioner No.1 to 3 and deceased Ranganathappa.
Upon going through the same, they prove the relationship of the deceased with the petitioner No.1 and 2.
The Aadhar card of the petitioner No.2 does not show her father's name.
However there is no dispute about the relationship.
Hence, it is held that the petitioner No.1 is wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children, as such they are the legal representatives of the deceased Ranganathappa.
17. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 57 years and his avocation is shown as Agriculturist and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Petitioners have not produced any document to prove the occupation and income of deceased.

In the absence of any documentary evidence before the Court to prove the income of the deceased, it is proper to take the notional income of the deceased Ranganathappa as Rs.16,000/- as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, since the said accident has been occurred in the year 2023.
18.
Further, the Petitioners stated the age of the deceased Ranganathappa was 57 years at the time of the accident.
They have produced Aadhar card of the deceased at Ex.P.15.
The Ex.P.6, shows the year of birth of the deceased is as 1966.
The accident was occurred on 13.02.2023.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Ranganathappa was 57 years.

Decided on 11.02.2025, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as follows:
"9.
We have heard the learned counsel for the Appellants.
We are unable to agree with the view taken by the Tribunal on the dependents of the deceased.

This court in National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender & Ors, had expounded that major married and earning sons of the deceased, being legal representatives, have a right to apply for compensation, and the Tribunal must consider the application, irrespective of whether the representatives are fully dependent on the deceased or not.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The court went on to conclude that since the sons, in that case, were earning merely Rs.1,50,000/- per annum, they were largely dependent on the earnings of the deceased and were staying with her.

10. Adverting to the facts at hand, on a perusal of the statement of Shashi Kumar, the son of the deceased (Appellant No.2 herein), annexed as Annexure P6, was working at a petrol pump, while the other son was involved in temporary employment opportunities only.
Both of them were residing with the deceased.
In such circumstances, it cannot be said that they were self-sufficient or independent of the deceased.
Similarly, applying the exposition in Birender (Supra), there is no reason to exclude a married daughter from compensation.
Therefore, in view of this, the High Court erred in excluding these dependents."
Underlined by me.
20. Keeping the aforesaid principle in mind, this Tribunal would proceed to decide the case on hand by considering the evidence available on record.
In the case on hand, admittedly the petitioner No.1 is the wife of deceased and she was completely dependent on the deceased.
The petitioner No.2 is the major son and petitioner No.3 is major daughter.
In the cross examination of PW.1 he admits that he has done ITI and doing agriculture.
He further admits that petitioner No.3 is married and residing with her husband.
He denied that he was not depending on his father.
Therefore, though the petitioner No.2 is doing agriculture, it cannot be said that he was self- sufficient or independent of the deceased.
Further as per the aforesaid authority, there is no reason to exclude a married daughter from compensation.
Hence, this Tribunal held that the petitioner No.2 and 3 are also considered as dependents of deceased.
21. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:

In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.

With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".
23.

This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
24.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased has left behind him, his wife, son and daughter.
Hence, the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are considered as dependents.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others).

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that : "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/-, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced @ 10% in every three years."
25. The Petitioner No.1 is wife of the deceased.
She has to live remaining part of her life in the absence of her husband.
The loss of husband full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to husband.
The Petitioner No.2 and 3 are children of the deceased.
They have to live remaining part of their life in the absence of their father.
The loss of father full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to father.
Therefore, petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- each under the head of loss of consortium and Rupees 16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rupees 16,500/- towards funeral expenses.

II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
26.
Petitioners are wife and children of the deceased and they lost their husband's love and care and father's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of these Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
27. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:
28.

It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was at Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that where the number of dependent of family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
In the case hand the dependents of member of deceased were 3, hence 1/3rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

Accordingly,
after deducting 1/3rd of the amount towards his personal expenses in Rs.17,600/- it comes to Rs.11,734/- (17,600 - 5,866) and multiplier applied is 9 which comes to Rs.12,67,272/- (Rs.11,734 x 12 x 9 = Rs.12,67,272/-) which is rounded off at Rs.12,67,300/-.
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.12,67,300/- towards loss of dependency.

In MFA No.1662/2023 (MV-D) between Chandrakala & another Vs Dilipkumar & another, Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that:
"Since the amount due under the head loss of future prospects is yet to become due, it would be illogical and illegal to direct the insurance company to pay interest on loss of future prospects.

entities.text: MFA No.1662/2023 (MV-D) between Chandrakala & another Vs Dilipkumar & another

sentences.text: Therefore, out of the total compensation payable, the respondent No.1 is not liable to pay any interest on the compensation under the head loss of future prospects."
In view of the said dictum, the amount awarded under the head loss of future prospects does not carry any interest.

Hence, the future prospect of 40% out of loss of dependency has been calculated in order to exclude interest which would comes at Rs.5,06,920/- i.e., ( 12,67,300 x 40/100 = 5,06,920/-).
32.

Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.14,92,300/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

33. Regarding Liability : As already discussed above, the petitioners have proved that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligence driving of the driver if Tanker Lorry bearing KA-20--C-6077.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle.
34. The respondent No.2 raised a contention that the vehicle involved in the accident is hazardous vehicle.
The person who drives hazardous vehicle must have specific driving licence.
The respondent No.1 who is the owner of the offending vehicle though very much present and contested the matter he did not bother to produce driving licence.
However, respondent No.2/insurer has summoned the concerned RTO to produce the extract of DL belongs to driver of the offending vehicle.
In response to the summons, the official of the RTO i.e., Shimoga RTO has produced Ex.R.2. wherein it shows that Hazardous goods vehicle license is valid from 18.10.2024.
But RW.1 deposed that the driver of lorry i.e., Sudhir.D was issued a Hazardous goods vehicle license for the first time on 28.02.2020.
There is no information in Ex.R.2 till which year the said license is valid.
However, the Hazardous License issued on 28.02.2020 is valid for a period of 3 years, i.e. till 27.02.2023.
The said license was renewed from 17.02.2023 to 16.02.2024.
Since the license of the said driver's heavy goods vehicle expires in the year 2024, the Hazardous Goods License will also expire in the same year.
In his cross-examination he has admitted that the driver of lorry i.e., Sudhir had a valid license to drive a hazardous goods vehicle on 13.02.2023.
Therefore, this Tribunal held that the driver of the offending vehicle had valid driving licence at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy at the time of accident to the offending vehicle.
Therefore, Respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the "Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".

35. Issue No.4 : From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.14,92,300/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents No.1 and 2 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.14,92,300/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.(The amount of Rs.5,06,920/- awarded under the head loss of future prospects does not carry any interest).
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.

Therefore, Respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
35. Issue No.4 : From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.14,92,300/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents No.1 and 2 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.14,92,300/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.(The amount of Rs.5,06,920/- awarded under the head loss of future prospects does not carry any interest).
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Compensation amount awarded to the Petitioners are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 70% to the Petitioner No.1 2) 15% each to the Petitioner No.2 & 3.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of E- payment after her proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
Since the apportion of petitioner No.2 and 3 is meager, entire amount awarded to petitioner No.2 and 3 shall be paid to them by way of E- payment after their proper identification.
